espn-604005.headline: England are favourites, which is the hard part
beats: Wales beat New Zealand 35–28 in Cardiff on 14 November, ending a run of 34 straight losses to them dating back 73 years. Matt Dawson's response was to name England favourites and to want them "absolutely bombarded" with the tag.

England have the case for it. They have won four straight, put 78 on Japan and 45 on Australia, and beat New Zealand 33–19 at home in their last meeting, on 15 November 2025. Three injured starters have been cleared to train.

New Zealand conceded 43 to South Africa in September and 35 to Wales in their last two defeats. Win this by 16 or more, though, and they go top of the world rankings, straight after one of the biggest shocks in Test history.
Eddie Jones has warned England to expect a "violent" response. Dawson wants to see how they carry being the side expected to win. This game tests both theories.

espn-604006.headline: Japan conceded 78 last week. Scotland scored 15.
beats: England had finished with Japan by the 20th minute at Twickenham, 78–15. It was their third straight loss, and the manner of it adds pressure on Eddie Jones a year out.

Scotland won ugly. They beat Australia 15–12 in the rain at Murrayfield with defence, a Finn Russell penalty six minutes from time, and Rory Darge as captain and player of the match. A week earlier, also at home, New Zealand put 43 past them.
Japan's last fortnight runs both ways: a seven-point loss to Wales, then a 63-point one at Twickenham. Win here by 16 or more and they go above Wales, Fiji and Italy.

Jack Dempsey scored Scotland's second try against Australia. In March he agreed a deal to leave Glasgow Warriors for club rugby in Japan, which put his Scotland future in serious doubt. If picked, he lines up against the country where he agreed to play his club rugby.

espn-604007.headline: Andrew Porter has had a year to think about this
beats: South Africa won in Dublin last November, 24–13, and Ireland's scrum had a miserable afternoon. As of early this month Andrew Porter had not played for Ireland since. His word for the rematch is "Swing at it".
Ireland's scrum dominated Argentina and Fiji in this window, but neither of them is South Africa. Andy Farrell's verdict on the 43–15 against Fiji was "I thought the scoreline flattered us a bit."

South Africa arrive off a 21–19 defeat in Paris, built on eleven entries into France's 22. Schalk Burger's view is that "they don't fear losing in the Springbok jumper." Lose a second in a row and they slip to second in the world, behind New Zealand.
Burger expects a response at the Aviva. Porter has spent a year preparing one of his own.

espn-604008.headline: Ten games, no wins, and somebody has to stop it
beats: Italy and Fiji meet at the foot of the Nations Championship, 0 from 5 each. Their points differences, minus 158 and minus 161, are the two worst in the competition, three apart.

Italy have lost six straight since beating England. The latest was 14–19 to Argentina in Genoa, where they could not use a two-man advantage in the second half. Danilo Fischetti expects a physical game and wants more discipline than last time.
Fiji conceded 54 to France and 43 to Ireland on consecutive weekends, though Andy Farrell said the margin flattered Ireland. Jake White's side last won in October, 34–28 in Japan.
Win in Udine and Italy go up to 9th in the world, above Fiji and Wales. Fiji's next Test after that is Spain at the World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to sit on a loss.

espn-604009.headline: France carry a one-point lead and an injury list home
beats: France lead the North by a point from England, and the North's top side plays the grand final. They got there by beating South Africa 21–19 after losing Marchand at the last minute and spending the evening going backwards at the scrum.

Argentina conceded 42 in Ireland, then held on 19–14 in Genoa against an Italy side with the means to win it late. An Argentina win at Stade de France would lift them above Australia in the world rankings and push France below England, which is the wrong side of England to be on this month.

Into that comes Matthieu Jalibert, recalled to an injury-hit squad of 42 after tearing his right quadriceps in September and relapsing in mid-October. A grand final place may rest on a fly-half who has not played in nearly two months.

espn-604010.headline: Wales beat New Zealand. Now for the follow-up
beats: Wales won 35–28 in Cardiff on 14 November, their first win over New Zealand since 1953. Sam Warburton and Dan Biggar ranked it among the biggest shocks in Test history.
Australia arrive on three straight defeats. They conceded 50 and 43 to that same New Zealand side and 45 in England. Wales put 35 past New Zealand with five tries.
Wales have won their last two at home, both with a four-try bonus. A third win would lift them to ninth in the world and push Australia down to eighth, below Argentina.
Steve Tandy has urged caution. Losing to the side that let in 45 at England would prove him right.
